alt: Looping animation of a hexagonal spiral lattice in orange and violet, two cells across, with three white triangle symbols marking the generators α, β and γ of its symmetry.
caption: The published animation: one period of 6.390159918584649 time units in 48 frames, two cells across. Drawn on it, as in the correspondence catalogue, are the three generators of its symmetry r33₁3₂. Each is a 120° anticlockwise turn about the point it marks, and the number beside it is what the turn costs, as a fraction of the period: about γ it changes nothing, about α it gives the film a third of a period later, about β two thirds later. At α and β the chemicals never move; the film turns around them.

alt: Stroboscopic animation, one frame per period. It begins as a sharp spiral lattice, slowly loses contrast over the first third, and ends as an almost flat field blinking in unison.
caption: Why you cannot simply simulate. This starts exactly on the published orbit, disturbed only by single-precision round-off, and simulates forward with the three zero-cost symmetries imposed at every step. One frame per period, 313 periods: the spirals fade, by period 135 none are left, and every point ends up oscillating in unison.
